accuracy.evidence: Statutory wording checked in DfE Relationships Education guidance (2019, updated 2025), 'Families and people who care for me' (other families sometimes look different but should be respected) and 'Respectful relationships' (respect others even when very different, e.g. physically or in background). Festival facts checked: diyas at Diwali, crescent new moon sighting starts Eid al-Fitr, red lanterns at Lunar New Year; every one involves special food and gathering with family. 'Cześć' is an informal Polish hello.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips named in PSHE Association guidance and the topic evidence: best friends must be alike in every way, someone who looks different shares nothing, a different way of eating or speaking is weird or wrong, and a real family needs a mum and a dad. Each appears as a prediction, a refused move in the Venn or house, or a tagged challenge answer.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagalike has mechanics no other lab uses: a two-circle Venn diagram where a dragged fact card lands in Mia only, Both or Sam only by drop position, a house you fill with people tiles and check against a description of who lives there, and a four-festival tray where only the two shared things are accepted. It models comparing two people, so relabelling would not turn it into another topic.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child sorts six cards and sees both piles fill, so friends are visibly same and different at once; 'Speaks English' must go in the middle even though Mia also speaks Polish; the house refuses to accept a dad for Kit and then calls two mums a family; and only food and family pass the festival test. The text confirms what the moves showed.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options: best friends are the same in every way (the pair sort shows three differences), speaking Polish puts 'Speaks English' only on Sam's side (the Venn refuses it), two mums is not a real family (the house builds it), and chopsticks are the wrong way to eat (only the curious reply is accepted).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions with distinct tags: 'none' and 'all' for the nothing-shared and identical slips, 'mum' for narrow family ideas, 'normal' and 'odd' for judging a language as abnormal or funny, 'side' and 'out' for Venn placement, and 'tree' for treating one festival's custom as shared.

readability.evidence: Family audience: learn/readability.py gives kid text FK grade -0.4 and adult text FK 9.3 (limits 5.0 and 10.0). Kid text uses short sentences with named children; adult text names the curriculum terms similarity, difference, respect, culture, family, celebration and Venn diagram, and the ELG for People, Culture and Communities.

no_filler.evidence: No filler pattern matched and explanation overlap with every lesson, including Different Lives and Experiences and Stereotypes and Individual Differences, stays under the 12 percent limit. Each kid paragraph shows one idea with a named child; adult paragraphs give the guidance, the tool, the named mistakes and the lab steps.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 390 px in light and dark themes for every step: the Same and Different boxes fill the lower canvas, the Venn labels sit inside each circle without clipping, the house tiles are a 3 by 2 grid of big targets, and the four festival names wrap inside their cards. walk.cjs passes on desktop and iPhone 13.

accessibility.evidence: axe reports no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in either theme; every canvas action has a large button (Same, Different, the three Venn zones, add or remove each person plus Done, each reply, each festival item) and the canvas aria-label is rewritten with every result. Show me completes all five tasks within the walk time limit.
